# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** It's rated IP68 and gets about 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost). It's also the top pick at What Hi-Fi and BestProducts, and the first choice at iTechGuides. Prices in the reviews run about $130 at Walmart to $150 at Amazon. [Buy links at What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) · [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

## Other picks by need

- **Budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 (about $65-80).** It's IP67, floats, and has 360-degree sound. Battery is about 14 hours, and it's small and quieter than the others. [Buy links at RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) · [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **Pool party: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, gets loud, and lasts 40+ hours. It's large and pricey, and its sound is directional. [Buy links at RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Mid-range, 360° sound: Ultimate Ears Epicboom.** It's IP67 and floats. Sound is consistent wherever you sit or swim, but battery is only about 15 hours. It's also Tom's Guide's best overall. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) · [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Small and easy to pack: JBL Grip (about $100).** It's IP68, under a pound, and shaped like a can. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester liked its bass and loudness. Its mesh body gets dusty. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Ultra-cheap: JBL Go 5 (about $40).** It's IP67, but battery is only about 8 hours. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)
- **Big and loud at a discount: Soundcore Boom 2 Plus.** It's 100 W, IPX7, floats, and runs up to 20 hours. It weighs 3.8 kg. The listed price is $249.99, or $200 with code AFSC20, which the site says it tested in Soundcore's cart on Oct 22. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus) (affiliate link)

## What to know before buying

- Look for IP67 or higher. For sandy beaches, the first number should be 5 or 6, as in IP67 or IP68. Soundcore's Boom 2 has no dust rating, so keep that one on a towel.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Close the charging-port flap, rinse with fresh water if the manual allows it, and dry the speaker before charging. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/))

I only have the review pages, not direct retailer product URLs, so the links above go to pages with current buy buttons (except Soundcore). Prices change, so check them at checkout.

If you tell me your budget and whether it's for a couple of people or a crowd, I can narrow it to one.
